WISHLY HOW-TO GUIDE · WEBSITE PRIVACY

How to Password Protect Your Wishly Website: A Complete Step-by-Step Guide

Want to share a birthday surprise, anniversary page or personal message with just the right people? Learn how Wishly’s optional website password works, how to turn it on before publishing, and how to manage access afterwards.

A published Wishly website normally opens for anyone who has its link. If you want an extra step before someone can see the page, you can set an optional password in the publishing screen. This guide explains the complete process—from choosing a password to helping your recipient unlock the website.

✦Wishly GuidePractical product guides · About this publication
Website privacy & security8 min readUpdated 17 November 2026

What does password protection do on a Wishly website?

When you set a password for a published Wishly website, visitors who open its link see a lock screen first. They must enter the correct password before the website content is delivered to that browser. This is useful for a personal birthday surprise, an anniversary message, a proposal page or another page that you do not want to leave openly accessible to every person who receives the URL.

Password protection is optional. If you leave the Website password field empty when publishing a new website, the page remains open to anyone who has its link, as it normally would.

Important: A password adds an access check, but it is not a guarantee that nobody can share the page. Anyone who has both the link and the password can open it and may pass them on. Do not publish highly sensitive information.

Before you begin

  • Sign in to the Wishly account that owns the website.
  • Create or open the website you want to publish.
  • Finish the content and check that the page is ready to share.
  • Choose a password that is easy for your intended recipient to enter but is not reused from your email, banking or other important accounts.

How to add a password before publishing

Follow these steps in the Wishly publishing flow. The wording may evolve as the product interface is updated, but the password control is labelled Password (optional).

  1. Open your website in the Builder. Choose the template, edit your message and finish the page as usual.
  2. Go to the publish step. When your website is ready, continue to the screen where you review its link and publishing settings.
  3. Find “Password (optional)”. Look below the link and preview settings for the Website password field.
  4. Enter your chosen password. Wishly accepts 4 to 64 characters. It cannot be blank or consist only of spaces. You can use the Show control to check what you typed, then hide it again.
  5. Publish the website. Press Publish website and wait for the publishing process to finish. For an existing website, press Update website after setting the password.
  6. Check the saved status. The publishing screen should show Password is on for a protected website.

How to share the link and password

Once publishing is complete, copy the website link and send it to the person you want to surprise. The recipient will see the lock screen when they open it. They need the password you chose to continue.

Share the link and password separately. For example, send the website link through WhatsApp and tell the recipient the password over a phone call or in a separate message on another channel. This way, a forwarded link by itself does not also reveal the password.

If you use Wishly’s Send link by email option, the email sends the website link but does not include the password. For a password-protected page, the email tells the recipient to ask you for the password. You must share it separately.

What does the visitor experience?

  1. The visitor opens your published Wishly URL.
  2. Instead of seeing the personal website immediately, they see a password lock screen.
  3. They type the password and submit it.
  4. If it is correct, Wishly loads the website content for that browser.
  5. If it is incorrect, the page remains locked and the visitor can try again later.

Wishly checks password attempts and applies rate limits to reduce repeated guessing. Too many attempts can temporarily prevent further tries, so ask the owner to confirm the password if the visitor is unsure rather than repeatedly guessing.

Will the visitor need to enter the password every time?

After a visitor enters the correct password, Wishly saves an unlock cookie for that particular website in that browser. The unlock can remain valid for up to 30 days, so the same person using the same browser does not have to type the password on every visit during that period.

Each website has its own unlock. Unlocking one protected Wishly website does not unlock another one. If the visitor changes browser or device, clears site cookies, or uses a different browser profile, they may be asked for the password again.

How to change an existing website password

  1. Sign in to the Wishly account that owns the published website.
  2. Open that website and go to its publishing step.
  3. If the password is already enabled, choose Change.
  4. Enter the new password in the field. Use 4–64 characters.
  5. Press Update website and wait for the update to complete.

The website keeps the same link when you change its password. However, changing the password invalidates earlier unlocks, so people who previously opened the page will need the new password the next time they access it.

How to remove password protection

  1. Open the website’s publishing step while signed in.
  2. When the screen shows Password is on, choose Remove.
  3. Confirm that the password will be removed when you update the website.
  4. Press Update website to save the change.

After the update, the page no longer asks visitors for a password. Anyone who has the link can open it. You might remove the password after a private surprise is over, but first consider whether you still want the page to be accessible to everyone with the URL.

How Wishly handles the password

There are a few important details behind the lock screen:

  • The password is not stored as readable text. Wishly stores a salted scrypt password hash. This means the saved value is a one-way hash rather than the original password.
  • The protected page content is fetched after unlocking. The protected website’s personal content is not included in the initial locked page. The browser requests it only after the correct password has been accepted.
  • Protected metadata is limited. Search engines and link previews are not given the private page title, description or personal content. The page uses a generic protected-website preview and is marked not to be indexed.
  • Unlocks are website-specific. Each website uses its own unlock cookie, and changing its password invalidates previous unlock tokens.
  • Repeated guesses are limited. Wishly applies rate limits to password attempts.

These measures are designed to keep the page behind its password prompt. They do not make a personal website a secure file vault or a place to store financial, identity, medical or other highly sensitive information.

Good password and sharing practices

  • Choose a password that is not easy to guess from a public birthday, name or anniversary date.
  • Do not reuse your email, social media or banking password.
  • Share the link and password through separate channels where practical.
  • Send the password only to the intended recipient or group.
  • If you think someone unintended has received the password, change it and update the website.
  • Remember that a recipient who can open the page may still take screenshots, save media or share the details with others.
  • Review the photos and text on the page before publishing. Password protection does not replace permission to use someone else’s photos or personal information.

Troubleshooting: common password problems

The website opens without asking for a password

Check whether the website is actually showing Password is on in the publishing step. If the password was entered but the website was not updated, the change may not have been saved. Also remember that a browser which has already been unlocked may continue to open the page without asking for the password for up to 30 days.

The password is not accepted

Check uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, spaces and punctuation. Passwords are case-sensitive. Ask the website owner to confirm the exact password. Avoid repeated guesses because Wishly applies attempt limits.

The visitor is asked for the password again

The visitor may be using another device or browser, may have cleared cookies, or the owner may have changed the password. Enter the current password again.

The owner cannot remember the password

Wishly does not show the original password back to the owner because it stores a one-way salted hash. The owner can open the publishing step, choose Change, set a new password and update the website. Then they should send the new password to the intended visitor.

Frequently asked questions

Is Wishly website password protection optional?

Yes. Leave the Website password field empty to publish a page that anyone with its link can open. Enter a password if you want visitors to unlock it first.

What is the minimum and maximum password length?

The current Wishly website password accepts 4 to 64 characters. Do not use a password that is only spaces.

Does the password change the website link?

No. Changing or removing the password does not require a new website link. Save the change by updating the website.

How long does an unlocked browser stay unlocked?

Up to 30 days for that particular website and browser, unless the password is changed or the browser’s relevant cookies are cleared.

Will Wishly email the password to my recipient?

No. The Send link by email feature sends the link only. If the website is password-protected, the email tells the recipient to ask the owner for the password.

Can I use the same password for several websites?

You can choose your own passwords, but using a different password for each website is a better practice, especially if you share the pages with different people.

Does a password prevent screenshots or forwarding?

No. It controls access to the page; it cannot stop someone who has opened the page from taking screenshots, saving information or sharing the password with someone else.

Wishly’s interface and features may change. This guide reflects the Wishly implementation reviewed on 17 November 2026. Always check the current publishing screen for the latest controls. Password protection is an access feature, not a guarantee of absolute privacy.
